title: Proof of concept proposal for Variant string-formatting.

milestone.title: 4.x
milestone.description: Issues and pull requests slated for an undetermined Godot 4 release.

body:
With an eye towards adding slot formatting to the [f-string implementation](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/103239), this PR implements a formatting configuration language similar to the [Python format specification mini-language](https://docs.python.org/3/library/string.html#formatspec). The core implementation is a new class FormatSpec that contains the formatting configuration, can parse a text description of that configuration, and can format a Variant using that configuration. I've also embedded this formatting into String::format so that you can specify a format spec in a format template (e.g. `"foo {0:#_x}".format([1234560])` -> `"foo 0x12_d680"`). And as mentioned above, if this is accepted I'd expect to integrate this into the f-string implementation to support embedded format strings (e.g. `f"foo {1234560:#_x}"`).

There is significant usage documentation attached to the [FormatSpec struct](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/compare/master...mpsalisbury:godot:string-format#diff-ecfadcb1f8fb1247111f44d736274558654e23a28afeecd131a9efddef8da1d9R760) (mirroring the Python spec), and many usage examples in [test_string.h](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/compare/master...mpsalisbury:godot:string-format#diff-d1036e3c844034f9afa5867e9266efe525bcd16c773be6b70a1d8deb83005bc0R2322).

## Some implementation notes

* This implementation leans towards the existing Godot string formatting patterns, such as supporting vector printing, rather than strictly following the Python patterns.
* I did not implement scientific or general floating point formatting. It would be easy to integrate those once we have precision-honoring implementations in String (for instance, while there is a String::num_scientific() method now, it currently calls sprintf with the 'g' format (not 'e'), and it doesn't accept a precision/decimals argument). 
* My integration with String::format leaves the existing support for placeholder templates alone and will only activate when the default placeholder `'{_}'` is used. This means that position-based placeholders (e.g. `{}`) and alternate keys (e.g. `$_`) will continue to work, just without the new formatting capabilities.

## Open Issues

* I have not yet looked into performance
* I have not yet looked into syntax highlighting
* I noticed that the existing vector formatting implementation considers that some platforms implement real_t as a float and some as a double. My platform (mac) uses a float, so I don't know how the implementation will work on a real_t==double platform. I presume the build/integration tests will reveal this.

Closes https://github.com/godotengine/godot-proposals/issues/2004
